newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SBC sees major growth in S.Africa telecoms.
newsitem.headline: SBC sees major growth in S.Africa telecoms.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc, selected on Monday along with partner Telekom Malaysia Bhd as sole bidder for a 30 percent stake in Telkom South Africa, said it saw major growth potential in the country.

"The expanding South African economy and significant unmet demand for high-quality telecommunications services represents an attractive growth opportunity," SBC chairman Edward Whitmore said in a statement.

State-owned Telkom has a countrywide franchise to provide local, domestic and international services. In addition, it owns a 50 percent stake in cellular network provider Vodacom. It reported $3.2 billion in revenues and $314 million in net income for the financial year ended March 31, 1996.
The sale of the strategic stake in Telkom to the SBC-Telekom Malaysia consortium marks the first major step in the South African government's privatisation programme.
A full announcement on the financial details of the transaction and the consortium's modernisation commitments will only be made once final negotiations are concluded, which is expected in April.
Analysts have estimated the value of the 30 percent stake at over $1.3 billion, valuing Telkom at more than $4 billion -- which they said made it the largest privatisation in Sub-Saharan Africa.
SBC, which reported 1996 revenues of $13.9 billion, has tens of millions of customers in 13 U.S. states and eight countries.
Telekom Malaysia, which was privatised in 1990, is the largest publicly-listed company in Malaysia. In 1996 it reported revenues of $2.6 billion.
